@@U02310@@
First let us celebrate Carnival and its merriment. Distractions wont help, but only keep us from our goal. We must compose ourselves first, do so in penitence, and having done so, earn the lower by means of the higher. Who wants the good must first be good; who seeks pleasure must tame his blood; who insists on wine must press ripe grapes; who longs for miracles must strengthen his faith.

@@U02312@@
Very well! We'll pass our time in merriment, and when Ash Wednesday comes it will be all the more welcome. So let’s celebrate Carnival all the more wildly.

@@U02313@@
(Trumpets. Exeunt all but 梅菲斯特.)

@@U02315@@
Luck and merit come as a pair in the human design; but little these fools know of that. If they held in hand the Philosopher's Stone, what good would it do them without a philosopher?
translation:
@@U02310@@
首先让我们庆祝狂欢节及其欢乐。分心不会有任何帮助，只会让我们偏离目标。我们必须首先让自己平静下来，以悔罪的态度这样做，然后通过较高的收入来赢得较低的收入。欲善者，必先为善；欲为善者，必先为善者。寻求快乐的人必须驯服他的血；谁坚持酿酒必须压熟葡萄；渴望奇迹的人必须坚定自己的信念。

@@U02312@@
很好！我们将在欢乐中度过我们的时光，当圣灰星期三到来时，我们将更加受到欢迎。因此，让我们更加疯狂地庆祝嘉年华吧。

@@U02313@@
（喇叭声。除梅菲斯特外，全部下场。）

@@U02315@@
人的设计中，运气与功绩是一对的；但这些傻瓜对此知之甚少。如果他们手中握有贤者之石，那么如果没有哲学家，这对他们有什么好处呢？
